outcome: No proof, disproof, bound, or credible claim regarding the infinitude of betrothed (quasi-amicable) numbers was found; the conjecture remains exactly as open as it was in January 2024. The only related activity found is a Lean formalization tracking issue and a Lean formalization paper, neither of which advances the mathematics.
summary: The Wikipedia article on betrothed numbers (checked as of this research) still lists the same known pairs as before and makes no claim about infinitude having been settled; it does not even frame infinitude as an explicit open question in its current text, but the mathematical literature and MathWorld both continue to treat it as unresolved. Two items of tangential activity were found in the window. First, a GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#2246, opened 2026-02-10 by user franzhusch) proposes formalizing the *statement* 'there are infinitely many betrothed pairs' as a target in the Lean/Mathlib-based formal-conjectures repository. The issue itself states 'This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me' — so an AI agent produced the issue text (identifying and phrasing the conjecture as a formalization target), but this is not mathematical content: it is a request to state an unproved conjecture in Lean, rated formalizability 2/5, and it explicitly is not a proof or partial proof of anything. No comments or follow-up work resolving it were found. Second, an arXiv preprint 'Formalization of Amicable Numbers Theory' (arXiv:2601.07444, Chen, Tang, Zhan) formalizes classical, already-known results about amicable, sociable, and betrothed numbers in Lean 4 (2076 lines, 139 theorems, zero `sorry`s) — including verified computational bounds (>10^65) and parity-constraint theorems — but its abstract gives no indication it proves or disproves infinitude of betrothed pairs; it is a formalization of existing mathematics, not new mathematics, and no AI/LLM involvement in producing the proofs is disclosed in the abstract. Under §3.1, neither item changes what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry: the first is a tracking issue for an AI-generated formalization *task*, not a result, and the second doesn't touch the infinitude question at all. No search turned up any preprint, blog post, or announcement claiming progress toward proving or disproving infinitely many betrothed number pairs exist since 26 January 2024.
competing_reading: One could argue the DeepMind formal-conjectures issue represents a form of 'AI activity' on this exact problem (an AI agent selected and phrased this specific open conjecture as noteworthy), which might be read as a very weak 'incident' of AI engagement. But per §6.2, identifying/phrasing a conjecture for a to-do list is not producing any mathematics that appears in a result — there is no result — so ai_role none and status open (not progress) is the correct reading.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint proving that infinitely many betrothed pairs exist (or do not), a proof that the set is finite, or even a partial/case result (e.g., infinitely many pairs within some restricted family) would move this off 'open'. Completion of the Lean formalization issue itself would not settle it, since the issue only asks for the conjecture's *statement*, not a proof.
